scenes.title: Eastward Journey and Notes
scenes.summary: Harker journals his rail journey from Munich through Vienna, Budapest and Klausenburgh toward Transylvania, noting food, delays, dreams, and his British Museum research on Transylvanian peoples and superstitions.

scenes.title: Dawdle Through Picturesque Country
scenes.summary: Harker's train dawdles all day through beautiful country, passing hill towns, castles, and rivers, while observing picturesque peasants and Slovaks at the stations.

scenes.title: Expected at the Golden Krone
scenes.summary: Harker reaches historic Bistritz at twilight and goes to the old-fashioned Golden Krone Hotel, where he is expected and receives Dracula's letter promising a diligence place and carriage at the Borgo Pass.

scenes.title: The Reticent Landlord
scenes.summary: Harker finds the landlord has secured his coach place by Dracula's letter, but the landlord turns reticent and evasive, and both he and his wife cross themselves in fear at Dracula's name and refuse to speak further.

scenes.title: The Landlady's Warning
scenes.summary: The old landlady hysterically begs Harker not to go on St. George's Eve when evil has full sway, and after failing to delay him, puts her crucifix around his neck for his mother's sake, leaving him uneasy as he waits for the coach.

scenes.title: Ominous Departure
scenes.summary: After dining on robber steak, Harker boards the diligence amid pitying stares, whispered words for Satan, hell, witch and vampire, and protective signs against the evil eye.

scenes.title: Haste Through the Blossoming Mittel Land
scenes.summary: Harker forgets his fears in the blossoming beauty of the Mittel Land as the coach flies with feverish haste over the rugged road toward Borgo Prund, past orchards, pine woods, and farmhouses.

scenes.title: Afternoon Light on the Lofty Carpathians
scenes.summary: Beyond the green hills the mighty forested slopes and snowy peaks of the Carpathians tower on both sides, glowing blue, purple, green, and brown in the afternoon sun with distant waterfalls gleaming in mountain rifts.

scenes.title: God's Seat and Cold Twilight Warnings
scenes.summary: At sunset a companion points out God's seat, then cold twilight closes in amid wayside crosses, kneeling peasants, weird pine woods, and mist; the driver refuses to let Harker walk, warning of fierce dogs.

scenes.title: The Borgo Pass Transfer
scenes.summary: At the Borgo Pass no carriage awaits until a black caleche with a towering, red-eyed driver appears; he seizes Harker's luggage with prodigious strength and drives in looping circles toward midnight.

scenes.title: Wolves and Blue Flames
scenes.summary: Dogs howl, then wolves close round the caleche while flickering blue flames appear by the road; the driver repeatedly vanishes to arrange stones, returning silently as the journey takes on nightmare repetition.

scenes.title: Ring of Terror and the Castle
scenes.summary: A visible ring of wolves encircles the horses in moonlight until the driver commands them back with a sweep of his arms; they vanish and the carriage ascends to the dark, ruined Castle Dracula.

scenes.title: Arrival in the Dark Courtyard
scenes.summary: Harker finds himself alone in a vast, gloomy courtyard. The driver helps him alight with prodigious strength, sets down his luggage by the great door, and then drives away into the darkness.

scenes.title: Waiting in Silence and Fear
scenes.summary: Left alone with no bell or knocker, Harker waits in endless silence, overcome by doubts and fears about where he is and what adventure he has begun, pinching himself to be sure he is awake among the Carpathians.

scenes.title: Welcome to My House
scenes.summary: The great door opens and the Count welcomes Harker with icy strength, then carries his luggage through stone passages to a warm, fire-lit suite.

scenes.title: Supper by the Fire
scenes.summary: Reassured by light and warmth, Harker sups on chicken and Tokay while the Count, who will not eat, reads Hawkins' letter and asks of the journey.

scenes.title: Children of the Night
scenes.summary: Studying his host by firelight, Harker is repelled by his pallor, sharp teeth, hairy palms and rank breath, then hears wolves as the Count calls them music of the night.

scenes.title: Morning Alone in the Castle
scenes.summary: Waking late next day to an absent host, Harker eats alone, notes the gold, lack of mirrors and servants, and finds a library full of English books.

scenes.title: To Speak England
scenes.summary: The Count declares his longing for London and warns Harker he may go anywhere except locked doors, then explains the blue flames of treasure-night and peasant fear.

scenes.title: The House at Carfax
scenes.summary: They review deeds for the Purfleet estate called Carfax, and the Count rejoices that it is old, large, and near a chapel, his smile turning malignant.

scenes.title: Rings on the Map
scenes.summary: Left alone Harker finds an atlas ringed at London, Exeter and Whitby, then talks late with the Count until cock-crow sends his host abruptly away at dawn.

scenes.title: No Reflection
scenes.summary: Shaving, Harker sees the Count has no reflection, bleeds, and recoils as the Count lunges for his throat but is stopped by his crucifix, then hurls the mirror away.

scenes.title: A Veritable Prison
scenes.summary: Exploring by day Harker sees magnificent precipices but finds every door locked, realizing with dread that the castle is a prison and he is a prisoner.

scenes.title: A Prisoner in the Castle
scenes.summary: Harker realizes he is a prisoner in the castle, calms his panic, and resolves to hide his fears while watching the Count, whose menial chores prove there are no servants.

scenes.title: The Pride of the House
scenes.summary: At midnight Harker questions the Count on Transylvania history. The Count warms wonderfully, speaking of battles as if present, explaining a boyar's pride in house and name, saying always 'we' like a king, growing excited and pacing as Harker listens fascinated.

scenes.title: Tales of Szekely Blood
scenes.summary: The Count delivers his fiery history of the Szekelys, from Ugric Berserkers and Huns and Attila's blood to driving back invaders, guarding the frontier, Cassova, the Dracula Voivode who beat the Turk, and later Draculas, ending that warlike glory is now a tale told. Near morning they retire to bed.

scenes.title: Questions of Business
scenes.summary: The Count questions Harker methodically about English solicitors, agents, and shipping consignments, displaying startling legal acumen.

scenes.title: Guarded Letters
scenes.summary: The Count forces Harker to agree to stay a month and to write only guarded business letters home. Harker writes formally while planning secret fuller accounts, then snoops on the Count's own stacked packets to Whitby, Varna, London, and Budapest before Dracula re-enters.

scenes.title: Warning Against Sleeping Elsewhere
scenes.summary: Left alone for the evening, Harker receives the Count's grave warning never to fall asleep outside his own rooms, lest bad dreams befall him. Harker later places the crucifix over his bed for protection.

scenes.title: The Crawling Man
scenes.summary: From a window Harker watches the Count crawl face-down down the castle wall like a lizard, then uses his absence to explore locked passages and a dusty ladies' wing.

scenes.title: Defiant Slumber
scenes.summary: Shaken and fearing for his sanity, Harker defies the Count's warning and settles to sleep in the moonlit old chambers, drifting into uneasy slumber.

scenes.title: Three Women in the Moonlight
scenes.summary: Alone in the moonlit room, Harker sees three beautiful women who cast no shadow approach him, whispering and laughing together as they urge the fair one forward, filling him with both burning desire and deadly fear.

scenes.title: This Man Belongs to Me
scenes.summary: As the fair woman kneels to feed on Harker's throat, the enraged Count intervenes, claims Harker as his own, promises him to them later, and placates them with a squirming bag containing something living; the women vanish into the moonlight and Harker loses consciousness.

scenes.title: Sanctuary and Splintered Door
scenes.summary: Harker wakes in his own bed unsure if the encounter with the vampire women was dream, finds small signs the Count carried him, and finds the upper room bolted from inside, confirming horror was real.

scenes.title: The Three Fatal Dates
scenes.summary: The Count in sweet tones forces Harker to write three postdated letters to cover his absence, fixing June 12, 19 and 29, and Harker realizes this is the span of his life.

scenes.title: Letters Thrown to the Szgany
scenes.summary: Hope revives when Szgany gipsies camp in the courtyard; Harker writes secret letters home, including one in shorthand to Mina, and throws them with gold through his barred window to be posted.

scenes.title: The Burning of the Secret Letter
scenes.summary: The Count calmly produces the intercepted letters, burns the unsigned shorthand letter in the lamp, returns the Hawkins letter for re-enveloping, locks Harker in, leaving him in despairing calm.

scenes.title: Stripped of Paper and Clothes
scenes.summary: Harker discovers every scrap of paper, notes, letter of credit, and even his travelling suit, overcoat and rug are gone, a new scheme to leave him helpless if he escapes.

scenes.title: The Empty Earth-Boxes Arrive
scenes.summary: Two great leiter-wagons drawn by eight horses arrive with empty rope-handled boxes; Harker finds his door locked from outside and his cries mocked and ignored.

scenes.title: The Crawling Man and Moon-Dust Women
scenes.summary: At night Harker watches the Count crawl lizard-like from his window in Harker's own clothes with the dreadful bag, then is hypnotized by moonlit dust coalescing into the three ghostly women before fleeing screaming to his lamp-lit room.

scenes.title: Monster, Give Me My Child
scenes.summary: A distraught peasant mother demands her child at the gate; the Count calls and wolves pour in and fall silent, and Harker understands her child's fate and his own helpless imprisonment.

scenes.title: Resolve to Climb the Wall
scenes.summary: With morning courage after his first postdated letter goes to post, Harker resolves on a desperate way: as the Count sleeps by day unseen, he will climb the wall and enter the Count's room by its window, bidding farewell to Mina.

scenes.title: The Chapel of Earth and Sleeping Count
scenes.summary: Harker creeps along the stone ledge into the empty, dusty Count's room, finds a heap of ancient gold, descends to a ruined chapel graveyard filled with earth-boxes, and finds the Count lying death-like in one box.

scenes.title: Welcome the Coming, Speed the Parting Guest
scenes.summary: The Count, seen again leaving by the window in Harker's clothes, invites Harker to depart at once, leads him to the great door only to open it upon howling wolves, forcing Harker to beg to wait till morning as the door slams and bolts.

scenes.title: Tonight Is Mine, Tomorrow Is Yours
scenes.summary: At his door Harker hears the Count stay the three terrible women with 'Tonight is mine. Tomorrow night is yours,' opens to their laughing, lip-licking faces, and falls to his knees as the end draws near.

scenes.title: Gorged With Blood and the Shovel Blow
scenes.summary: At dawn Harker scales the wall again, finds the great box lid unfixed and the Count bloated ruby-red and gorged with fresh blood; he madly strikes with a shovel, gashing the forehead before the lid falls and hides the grinning thing.

scenes.title: Nailed Down and Left Alone
scenes.summary: Trapped again as Szgany and Slovaks nail down the boxes and depart, Harker is left alone with the awful women and resolves to take gold, scale the castle wall to the precipice, and flee home or die as a man.

scenes.title: Mina's Longing Letter
scenes.summary: Mina writes to Lucy longing to be together by the sea, practising shorthand and typing to help Jonathan, noting Jonathan is well in Transylvania and will return soon.

scenes.title: Lucy's Secret Love Confession
scenes.summary: Lucy teases Mina about correspondence, describes Mr. Holmwood and Dr. Seward, then secretly confesses she loves Arthur and blushes as she writes for sympathy and prayers.

scenes.title: Three Proposals - Dr. Seward Refused
scenes.summary: Lucy announces three proposals in one day, then recounts Dr. Seward's nervous, straightforward proposal before lunch and her painful refusal while loving another, leaving her miserable yet happy.

scenes.title: Quincey's Jolly American Proposal
scenes.summary: That evening Lucy tells Mina how Quincey Morris found her alone after lunch, nervous yet jolly, amusing her with American slang before proposing in harness-driving terms, which she lightly refuses, leading him to turn suddenly earnest in a torrent of lovemaking.

scenes.title: Quincey Morris's Noble Farewell
scenes.summary: Morris nobly asks if she cares for another and vows to be only a faithful friend if so; Lucy tearfully confesses she loves someone else, he praises her honesty and pluck, asks for one farewell kiss to keep off the darkness, wrings her hand and leaves without looking back, leaving her crying with guilt at his heartbreak.

scenes.title: Number Three - Arthur's Embrace
scenes.summary: In a blissful postscript Lucy reveals number Three was Arthur, whose sudden embrace and kisses have made her very happy and grateful to God for lover, husband, and friend.

scenes.title: Seward's Gloom and Renfield Study
scenes.summary: Seward turns to his phonograph diary after his rebuff, restless and empty, and coldly interrogates his quaint patient Renfield to master the facts of his fixed idea and dangerous temperament.

scenes.title: A Toast to the Happy Rival
scenes.summary: Quincey invites Arthur and Jack Seward to his campfire to drink to the happiest man who won the noblest heart, and Arthur wires back accepting with tingling news to share.

scenes.title: Arrival at Whitby and the Churchyard View
scenes.summary: Mina arrives in Whitby, met by Lucy, and describes the Esk valley, viaduct, red-roofed old town, ruined abbey with White Lady legend, and the parish churchyard cliff with its fallen graves and fine view over the harbour, where she writes while three old men talk beside her.

scenes.title: The Harbour Description and the Sceptical Old Sailor
scenes.summary: Mina describes the harbour piers, lighthouses, tidal sands, reef and bell-buoy, then meets a gnarled nearly-hundred-year-old ex-Greenland sailor who brusquely dismisses the sea-bells and White Lady legends, leaves for tea with his granddaughter, and Mina notes the long church steps before going home.

scenes.title: Old Swales Sermon on Lying Tombstones
scenes.summary: On the cliff with Lucy, Mina draws old Swales out on legends; he preaches that ghosts and tombstone inscriptions are lies, citing empty sailor graves and the suicide George Canon.

scenes.title: Seat Over a Suicide's Grave
scenes.summary: Lucy is horrified to learn her favourite seat is over a suicide's grave, while the old man reassures her it is harmless before leaving.

scenes.title: Marriage Talk and Lonely Night Watch
scenes.summary: Lucy renews talk of Arthur and their marriage, leaving Mina heartsick for Jonathan; later alone at night Mina watches the town lights and longs for him.

scenes.title: Renfield's Rising Chain of Lives
scenes.summary: Seward tracks Renfield's ascending chain of live prey from flies to spiders to sparrows to a demanded cat, culminating in the discovery he has eaten his birds raw and drugging him to examine his notebook.

scenes.title: Seward's Zoophagous Classification
scenes.summary: Seward gives Renfield a strong opiate and examines his pocketbook, confirming his theory that Renfield is a zoophagous life-eating maniac who cumulatively absorbs lives from flies to spiders to birds. He muses on completing the experiment and advancing brain science, while resisting temptation without sufficient cause.

scenes.title: Seward's Hopeless Longing
scenes.summary: Seward admires Renfield's consistent reasoning and new record, contrasting it with his own life ended with lost hope for Lucy. Unable to be angry with Lucy or his successful friend, he resolves to wait hopelessly and work, envying Renfield a strong unselfish cause for happiness.

scenes.title: Anxiety over Jonathan and Sleepwalking Lucy
scenes.summary: Mina grows anxious over Jonathan's strange brief letter from Castle Dracula and silence, while Lucy sleepwalks nightly, tries locked doors, and awaits her postponed meeting with Holmwood.

scenes.title: Foreboding Wind and Strange Ship
scenes.summary: Under a grey brewing storm, the repentant old Swales senses death in the wind and bids Mina farewell, then the coastguard points out a strangely steered Russian ship drifting toward harbour.

scenes.title: Calm Before the Great Storm
scenes.summary: A Whitby correspondent sets the scene of a sultry August holiday turned ominous, with mares'-tails, dead calm, oppressive silence, and a foreign schooner with all sails set idling offshore.

scenes.title: The Tempest Breaks
scenes.summary: Without warning the tempest breaks with roaring wind, mountainous seas, sea-fog, and lightning, while the new East Cliff searchlight guides struggling fishing-boats to safety amid cheers.

scenes.title: The Schooner Finds the Harbour
scenes.summary: The strange schooner with all sails set rushes before the blast between the piers and beaches herself on Tate Hill Pier, found to have been steered only by a corpse lashed to the helm.

scenes.title: The Dog Ashore and the Dead Helmsman
scenes.summary: An immense dog springs from below and vanishes toward the churchyard cliff, while the coastguard, correspondent, and surgeon examine the crucifix-bound steersman dead two days with his bottled log, as the storm abates.

scenes.title: Sequel of the Demeter
scenes.summary: The wreck is identified as the Russian Demeter from Varna carrying silver sand and boxes of mould, the landing dog has vanished after a savage night killing, and the Board allows publication of its strange log.

scenes.title: First Disappearances at Sea
scenes.summary: The captain's log begins with routine departures through the Bosphorus and Mediterranean, then turns to unease as Petrofsky vanishes and Olgaren sees a tall thin stranger aboard, leading to a fruitless stem-to-stern search.

scenes.title: Doom Closes Round the Ship
scenes.summary: Fog, tempest, and relentless loss consume the Demeter man by man through Biscay and the Channel, until the maddened mate stabs at an unseen Thing in the hold and throws himself overboard, leaving the captain to lash his own hands with crucifix to the wheel.

scenes.title: Hero's Funeral Decreed
scenes.summary: With an open verdict and no explanation for the murders, Whitby hails the dead captain as a hero and plans a great public funeral up the Esk to the cliff churchyard, while the great dog remains unfound.

scenes.title: Lucy's Restless Night
scenes.summary: In her journal Mina recounts a fearful storm night of Lucy's restless sleepwalking and undressing, then a bright anxious morning visit to the torn harbour while fearing for Jonathan's whereabouts.

scenes.title: Funeral Shadows and Foreboding
scenes.summary: At the touching harbour funeral near their seat, Lucy is deeply upset by old Mr. Swales found dead with horror on his face and by a dog turned furious then terrified at the tombstone, prompting Mina to plan an exhausting cliff walk to prevent sleepwalking.

scenes.title: A Happy Evening in Whitby
scenes.summary: Mina closes a happy day in Whitby: a walk, fright from cows, hearty tea at Robin Hood's Bay, and Lucy asleep looking sweet and improved. Mood is warm, domestic contentment.

scenes.title: Midnight Search at St. Mary's
scenes.summary: Waking to find Lucy's bed empty, Mina searches Whitby by moonlight and finds her half-reclining on the churchyard seat with something long, black, bending over her with a white face and red gleaming eyes. Terror and supernatural menace dominate.

scenes.title: Bringing Lucy Home Unseen
scenes.summary: Mina wraps the sleeping Lucy in a shawl, fastening it with a safety-pin, wakes her gently, and sneaks her home barefoot and unseen. They wash, pray, and swear secrecy to protect her mother and reputation. Mood is tender, anxious relief.

scenes.title: Fragile Recovery
scenes.summary: Lucy looks better in the morning despite tiny pierced wounds on her throat from the pin. A bright day at Mulgrave Woods and music follows, though Lucy twice tries to leave in her sleep. Mood is fragile, deceptive calm.

scenes.title: Bat, Red Eyes, and the Windowsill
scenes.summary: Ominous signs accumulate: a great bat flitting at the moonlit window, Lucy's remark about 'His red eyes again' at sunset, a bird-like shape on her windowsill as she sleepwalks, and growing pallor and haggardness. Mood turns uncanny and watchful.

scenes.title: Consent to Marry and a Secret Death Warrant
scenes.summary: Arthur's father's improvement brings consent for a soon marriage, filling Lucy with quiet joy. Mrs. Westenra is glad and sorry at once, confiding in secret that her heart is failing and she has only months to live, and that shock could kill her.

scenes.title: Lucy's Fading Strength and Unhealed Wounds
scenes.summary: A shadow falls over their happiness with no news from Jonathan. Despite eating and sleeping well, Lucy fades daily, languid and pale, gasping at night and found faint at the open window. Her throat wounds remain open, larger, with faintly white edges.

scenes.title: Fifty Boxes for Carfax
scenes.summary: Cold business correspondence arranges urgent rail shipment of fifty boxes to the ruined chapel at Carfax near Purfleet, with keys left in the hall. Mood is bureaucratic and chillingly impersonal.

scenes.title: Bright Again on the Churchyard Seat
scenes.summary: Mina writes happily from the churchyard seat where she once found Lucy asleep. Lucy has slept well and seems bright, cheerful, and like her old self again, playfully tapping the stone slab.

scenes.title: A Dream of Dogs, Red Eyes, and Green Water
scenes.summary: Prompted about that night, Lucy half-recalls in a dreamy way passing streets and bridge amid howling dogs, something long and dark with red eyes, sinking in green water, and her soul floating free before Mina woke her. Mina finds it uncanny and steers to happier talk.

scenes.title: Joy at Last News
scenes.summary: Mina rejoices at last having news of Jonathan. Learning he has been ill, she treasures Sister Agatha's letter, arranges to leave in the morning to nurse him and bring him home, with Mr. Hawkins kindly suggesting they might marry out there.

scenes.title: Sister Agatha's Letter
scenes.summary: Sister Agatha writes from Budapest on behalf of Jonathan, who is too weak to write. She reports nearly six weeks of violent brain fever, now progressing well, his regrets to Mr. Hawkins, completed work, need for rest in the hills, and wish to pay for his care.

scenes.title: Warning of Delirium
scenes.summary: In a postscript, Sister Agatha confides Jonathan suffered some fearful shock, raving in delirium of wolves, blood, ghosts and demons, and urges gentleness lest he be excited. She reassures Mina he is well cared for, beloved, and recovering.

scenes.title: The Master Is at Hand
scenes.summary: Seward records Renfield's sudden evening excitement and haughtiness toward the attendant and himself, with talk that the Master is at hand, which Seward reads as threatening religious mania.

scenes.title: The Bride Draweth Nigh
scenes.summary: Renfield disdains his spiders and pets with cryptic talk of bride-maidens dimming as the bride draws nigh, then Seward closes wearily thinking of Lucy and sleeplessness.

scenes.title: Escape to the Chapel Door
scenes.summary: Renfield escapes naked through his window to the deserted Carfax house, pressing against the chapel door and pleading as a faithful slave for reward. Recaptured and chained, he whispers it is coming. Mood is frantic horror resolving into grim containment.

scenes.title: Mina Finds Jonathan in Budapest
scenes.summary: Mina writes to Lucy from Budapest that she has found Jonathan thin, pale, and broken after brain fever, with no memory of his long absence. Sister Agatha reassures her his ravings were of horrors, not of shame. Waking, Jonathan solemnly gives Mina his sealed notebook to keep unread unless stern duty requires it, affirming perfect trust between husband and wife.

scenes.title: Wedding in the Hospital Chapel
scenes.summary: Mina describes her wedding in the hospital: Jonathan answers his vows firmly from his sickbed. Alone together, she wraps his notebook in white paper, ties it with blue ribbon, and seals it with her wedding ring as a sign of trust. Solemn and happy as a new wife, she blesses Lucy and signs herself Mina Harker.

scenes.title: Lucy's Cheerful Reply
scenes.summary: Lucy replies cheerfully from Whitby, claiming restored health, good sleep and appetite, and joyful days with Arthur. She adds her mother seems better and that she and Arthur are to marry on 28 September.

scenes.title: Renfield's Moonlit Calm
scenes.summary: Seward records Renfield's strange cycle of daytime violence and calm from moonrise to sunrise. Renfield escapes to the deserted house chapel, grows furious then suddenly calm while watching a straight-flying bat in the moonlit sky.

scenes.title: Lucy's Failing Nights
scenes.summary: Lucy's diary turns dark and fearful. She dreams as at Whitby, remembers nothing, feels weak, pale and short of breath, hears scratching at the window, and wishes to sleep in her mother's room.

scenes.title: Arthur's Plea for Help
scenes.summary: Alarmed by Lucy's rapid decline, Arthur begs Seward to see her secretly at Hillingham, then wires that he is summoned to his worsening father and asks for a full report by post.

scenes.title: Seward's Baffling Examination
scenes.summary: Seward reports examining Lucy: gay before her mother but collapsed alone, pale and bloodless yet with normal blood analysis, troubled breathing and frightening dreams. Baffled, he has summoned his master Van Helsing.

scenes.title: Van Helsing Is Coming
scenes.summary: Van Helsing answers at once that he is already coming to London, asking for rooms at the Great Eastern and a meeting with the young lady the next day, out of friendship and duty.

scenes.title: The Professor's Grave Reticence
scenes.summary: Seward describes Van Helsing's careful, genial examination of a seemingly improved Lucy. Van Helsing finds no functional cause yet admits much blood has been lost, remains gravely reticent, and promises to think and return if needed.

scenes.title: Renfield Deserts His Flies
scenes.summary: Renfield swings violently at noon and sunset, then abruptly discards flies, sugar and spider-hunting, declaring he is deserted. Seward wonders if sun, like moon, exerts a malign influence on certain natures.

scenes.title: Telegrams of Hope and Alarm
scenes.summary: Three brisk telegrams chart false hope — Lucy better, greatly improved — then a terrible sudden change for the worse, with Seward urgently summoning Van Helsing at once.

scenes.title: A Guarded Letter
scenes.summary: Seward writes to Arthur that Lucy has relapsed, but that Mrs. Westenra has agreed to let Van Helsing jointly take charge, allowing them to act without alarming her.

scenes.title: Caution at Liverpool Street
scenes.summary: Van Helsing meets Seward at Liverpool Street, warns him to tell Arthur nothing yet, and speaks in parables about sown corn, urging careful record-keeping because Lucy's case may prove of great interest.

scenes.title: No Time to Be Lost
scenes.summary: Seward and Van Helsing find Lucy chalk-pale and struggling to breathe; Van Helsing declares there is no time to lose and that she must have an immediate transfusion of blood.

scenes.title: The Lover's Offer
scenes.summary: Arthur arrives unexpectedly in an agony of anxiety; Van Helsing seizes on his youth and strength, persuading the lover to give his own blood to save Lucy.

scenes.title: Blood for Blood
scenes.summary: Under narcotic sleep the transfusion restores color to Lucy's cheeks while draining Arthur; as Van Helsing settles her pillow, Seward glimpses a red mark on her throat beneath her velvet band.

scenes.title: The Punctures over the Jugular Vein
scenes.summary: After Arthur leaves, Seward returns to find Lucy breathing stronger with Van Helsing watching her. He loosens the velvet band and discovers two small punctures over her external jugular vein, white and worn at the edges, and puzzles over them as an impossible explanation for her great loss of blood.

scenes.title: The Charge to Keep Watch
scenes.summary: Unable to explain the mark, Seward listens as Van Helsing says he must go back to Amsterdam that night for books. He charges Seward to keep watch over Lucy all night without sleeping, and leaves with a solemn warning never to let her out of his sight.

scenes.title: The Night Watch
scenes.summary: Seward keeps an all-night vigil while Lucy fears sleep as a presage of horror; she sleeps deeply and peacefully, wakes renewed, and Seward wires good news to Van Helsing and Arthur.

scenes.title: The Weary Watcher Sleeps
scenes.summary: Exhausted after two sleepless nights, Seward arrives at Hillingham to find Lucy up and cheerful. She insists he must not sit up and installs him on the sofa in the room next to hers with doors open, and he promptly falls asleep.

scenes.title: Sunshine After Weakness
scenes.summary: Lucy writes happily in her diary, rejoicing in returning strength, feeling Arthur very close to her, and comforted that Seward is watching nearby so she need not fear to sleep.

scenes.title: All Work Undone
scenes.summary: Wakened by Van Helsing at dawn, Seward finds Lucy horribly white and corpse-like again, all their prior work undone. Seward gives his own blood in a second transfusion while Van Helsing uses morphia to keep Lucy asleep.

scenes.title: Nothing Must Be Said
scenes.summary: Van Helsing swears Seward to secrecy about the transfusion, sends him to rest and eat. Seward puzzles over how Lucy lost so much blood and the punctures in her throat as Lucy sleeps on into the day.

scenes.title: Strict Injunctions
scenes.summary: Lucy revives unaware of what happened; Van Helsing walks to telegraph, then orders Seward home to eat and strengthen himself while he himself will sit up with Lucy and let no others know.

scenes.title: Garlic and Silence
scenes.summary: Van Helsing receives garlic flowers from Haarlem, sternly forbids mockery, seals windows, door and fireplace with garlic and hangs a wreath round Lucy's neck, confident his 'spell' will hold the night.

scenes.title: Lucy's Garlic Peace
scenes.summary: Lucy records feeling comforted and sleepy among Van Helsing's garlic flowers, no longer dreading the night or flapping at the window.

scenes.title: A Bright Morning Turned Wrong
scenes.summary: Seward and Van Helsing arrive at Hillingham on a bright autumn morning to hear Lucy is better, until Mrs. Westenra proudly admits she removed the garlic flowers and opened the window.

scenes.title: Van Helsing Breaks Down
scenes.summary: Once Mrs. Westenra leaves, Van Helsing collapses in despairing sobs, lamenting that the well-meaning mother has doomed her daughter body and soul.

scenes.title: Locking the Door for Blood
scenes.summary: Van Helsing finds Lucy again waxen and pale, locks the door, and lays out instruments for another transfusion, stopping the weakened Seward from giving blood and insisting that Seward operate while he himself provides it.

scenes.title: Revival and Doubt
scenes.summary: The operation restores Lucy's colour and healthy sleep; Van Helsing warns Mrs. Westenra to leave the flowers untouched, takes over the night watch, and after Lucy wakes fresh and bright, Seward wonders if his work among the insane is unsettling his own mind.

scenes.title: Four Days of Recovery
scenes.summary: Lucy reports four days and nights of peace, growing strong, free of flapping and voices, fond of garlic, as Van Helsing prepares to leave for Amsterdam.

scenes.title: Tea With the Wolf-Keeper
scenes.summary: A Pall Mall Gazette interviewer coaxes the Zoo wolf-keeper Thomas Bilder over tea into talking about the escaped wolf Bersicker.

scenes.title: Bersicker and the Red-Eyed Visitor
scenes.summary: Bilder tells how Bersicker raged at the bars before a tall thin man with red eyes and white teeth stroked him, after which the wolf lay watchful and still.

scenes.title: Simply Because He Wanted Out
scenes.summary: Asked about other witnesses and the escape, Bilder dismisses the gardener's tale of a big grey dog as drink-inspired, then jokes that the wolf escaped simply because he wanted out, a well-worn sell that makes him and his wife laugh.

scenes.title: Hiding, Hungry, and Dangerous
scenes.summary: Prompted by the promise of a second half-sovereign, Bilder gives his real opinion: the tame, unfighting wolf is hiding and shivering, likely seeking food in a cellar or butcher's shop, and could threaten an infant left alone in a perambulator.

scenes.title: The Wolf Comes Home
scenes.summary: Bersicker suddenly returns of his own accord, cut and glass-wounded from climbing a wall, and is tenderly caged and fed like a penitent prodigal son.

scenes.title: The Blood Is the Life
scenes.summary: Renfield bursts into Seward's study with a dinner-knife, cuts Seward's wrist, then licks the spilled blood from the floor chanting 'The blood is the life!'

scenes.title: A Night Lost
scenes.summary: A delayed telegram from Van Helsing ordering flowers be kept in place fills Seward with dismay at a lost night, and he rushes for the train to London.

scenes.title: Lucy's Night Watch Begins
scenes.summary: Lucy leaves a written record, weak and fearing death, telling how she placed the flowers, fell asleep, then woke to flapping, howling, and a bat at the window.

scenes.title: The Wolf at the Window
scenes.summary: Mrs. Westenra joins Lucy in bed when a grey wolf crashes through the window; she tears away Lucy's garlic wreath, dies of fright, servants are found drugged with laudanum, and Lucy is left alone with the dead amid dust-specks and blue flames.

scenes.title: The Silent House and Forced Entry
scenes.summary: Seward arrives at Hillingham to silence, fears the worst, meets Van Helsing at the gate, and they break in through a barred kitchen window to find the servants drugged with laudanum.

scenes.title: Race Against Death to Save Lucy
scenes.summary: Inside Lucy's room they find Mrs. Westenra dead and Lucy near death with bare throat; Van Helsing declares it not too late and they revive her with brandy, heat, and a hot bath.

scenes.title: Quincey Morris Arrives
scenes.summary: Downstairs Van Helsing admits they need blood at once and have no donor, when Quincey Morris speaks from the sofa. Summoned by Arthur Holmwood's telegram about Lucy, Quincey offers himself, and Van Helsing welcomes him as God-sent help.

scenes.title: The Second Transfusion
scenes.summary: They perform another ghastly transfusion, which revives Lucy less well than before until morphia sends her faint into profound slumber. Afterwards Van Helsing finds a paper that dropped from Lucy's breast.

scenes.title: The Mysterious Note and What Took the Blood
scenes.summary: Van Helsing puzzles over a note dropped from Lucy's breast while Seward arranges the death certificate; Quincey presses Seward, linking Arthur's decline to vampire bats draining blood.

scenes.title: Lucy Wakes and Fades
scenes.summary: Lucy wakes, grieves her mother, then sleep-tears the paper; through the next day she weakens despite watching, and Arthur is telegraphed for as the watchers fear the end.

scenes.title: Mina's Happy News from Exeter
scenes.summary: Mina writes joyfully of Jonathan's return, their welcome by Mr. Hawkins, his gift of home and inheritance, and asks for Lucy's wedding news.

scenes.title: Renfield Attacks the Box Carriers
scenes.summary: Dr. Hennessey reports Renfield's cunning outbreak and furious attack on two carriers delivering great wooden boxes to the empty house next to the asylum.

scenes.title: Mina's Blow - Hawkins Dead
scenes.summary: Mina writes again in sorrow that Mr. Hawkins has died suddenly, leaving Jonathan burdened and shaken, and she must come to London for the burial.

scenes.title: Seward's Night Watch and the Bat at the Window
scenes.summary: Seward relieves Van Helsing on night watch over Lucy while Arthur rests; he notes her stertorous breathing, lengthened canine teeth, and garlic chaplet, sees a great bat buffeting the moonlit window, and finds Lucy has torn the garlic from her throat.

scenes.title: Morning Relief and the Vanished Wounds
scenes.summary: Through the night Lucy alternately discards the garlic while lethargic and clutches it when awake; at six Van Helsing relieves Seward, removes the flowers and handkerchief, and both men are horrified to find the throat wounds have absolutely disappeared.

scenes.title: Lucy's Deathbed and Forbidden Kiss
scenes.summary: Dying, Lucy receives Arthur; her manner turns voluptuous and predatory as she invites his kiss, Van Helsing hurls him back, then she returns gently to bless them and dies.

scenes.title: Peace Denied - Only the Beginning
scenes.summary: Arthur sobs while Van Helsing watches Lucy's corpse regain beauty; to Seward's claim of peace, Van Helsing solemnly warns it is only the beginning.

scenes.title: Funeral Formalities Arranged
scenes.summary: Seward attends to the ghastly formalities for the joint burial of Lucy and her mother the next day, while Van Helsing stays conspicuously close and insists on examining Lucy's papers himself.

scenes.title: Secret Papers Secured
scenes.summary: Van Helsing reveals his legal knowledge and his torn memorandum from Lucy's breast, has Seward seal Mrs. Westenra's papers for her solicitor, and secures Lucy's letters, memoranda, and new diary to keep her thoughts from strangers.

scenes.title: The Beautiful Corpse
scenes.summary: Seward and Van Helsing view Lucy's unnaturally beautiful corpse; Van Helsing places wild garlic and his gold crucifix on her before restoring the shroud.

scenes.title: The Post-Mortem Knives
scenes.summary: Alone in Seward's room, Van Helsing asks him to bring post-mortem knives to cut off Lucy's head and remove her heart after Arthur has seen her, shocking Seward who calls it monstrous mutilation of the dead.

scenes.title: A Plea for Faith
scenes.summary: Van Helsing pleads for blind trust on past faith, warning of strange and terrible days ahead and begging Seward to stand as one with him so he need not work lonely and heavy-hearted.

scenes.title: Devotion by the Bier
scenes.summary: Seward gives his promise and watches Van Helsing retire, then is moved to see a maid slip alone into Lucy's room to keep devoted watch by her mistress's bier through the night.

scenes.title: The Stolen Crucifix
scenes.summary: At dawn Van Helsing cancels the operation as too late, revealing his crucifix was stolen in the night by the maid who watched Lucy, leaving a new mystery.

scenes.title: The Solicitor's Comfort
scenes.summary: The solicitor settles Mrs. Westenra's estate, leaving all to Arthur, then Seward and Van Helsing prepare the death-chamber holding mother and daughter for Arthur's arrival.

scenes.title: Arthur's Farewell
scenes.summary: Broken Arthur breaks down with Seward, then kisses Lucy goodbye, disturbed by her lifelike loveliness and whispering doubt whether she is really dead.

scenes.title: Forgiveness at Dinner
scenes.summary: Over dinner Van Helsing remains silent until cigars, when Arthur stops him from using his title out of fresh grief. Van Helsing gently says he has grown to love him as Arthur, and Arthur takes his hand, asks to be friends, and begs forgiveness for his earlier rudeness.

scenes.title: Trust and Lucy's Papers
scenes.summary: Van Helsing tells Arthur he cannot yet trust or understand him, but will one day bless him for it. Arthur pledges complete trust, and Van Helsing asks permission to keep and read all of Lucy's papers and letters, safe from strange hands, to return in good time for a motive she would have approved.

scenes.title: Vigil by the Coffin
scenes.summary: Arthur heartily grants Van Helsing leave to do what he will without question, as Lucy would have wished. Van Helsing solemnly warns of pain and bitter water ahead, then patrols all night by Lucy's garlic-strewn coffin while Seward sleeps on a sofa in Arthur's room.

scenes.title: A Quiet Funeral in Exeter
scenes.summary: Mina journals on the train to Exeter and recalls Hawkins's simple solemn funeral, feeling their best friend is gone.

scenes.title: The Man Himself in London
scenes.summary: Walking in London, Jonathan is terrified to recognize the beaky, red-lipped dark man watching a girl as the Count himself, grown young, then falls asleep and forgets.

scenes.title: News of Double Loss
scenes.summary: Home to an empty house and Jonathan's relapse, Mina receives Van Helsing's telegram that Mrs. Westenra and Lucy died and were buried that day.

scenes.title: King Laugh at the Grave
scenes.summary: After the burial Arthur and Quincey leave, Van Helsing swings between hysterical King Laugh and tears, explaining his grim irony about transfusions, and Seward closes his diary in hopeless loneliness.

scenes.title: A Hampstead Mystery
scenes.summary: The Westminster Gazette reports children around Hampstead Heath straying late in the evening and claiming they were with a 'bloofer lady,' dismissed as a popular children's game.

scenes.title: The Hampstead Horror
scenes.summary: The paper notes all night-missing children have small throat wounds, police are put on lookout, and another weak, emaciated child is found at Shooter's Hill with the same wound after being lured by the 'bloofer lady.'

scenes.title: Mina Reads Jonathan's Journal
scenes.summary: Mina reads Jonathan's foreign journal in private, is shaken by its horrors, doubts its truth, and resolves to typewrite it so she can speak for Jonathan and spare him.

scenes.title: A Plea for Help
scenes.summary: Van Helsing writes in confidence asking Mina's help about Lucy, and Mina telegraphs back inviting him to come at once by morning train.

scenes.title: Anticipation Before the Visit
scenes.summary: Mina anxiously awaits Van Helsing, convincing herself his visit concerns Lucy's sleepwalking, and prepares her typewritten account to answer his questions.

scenes.title: A Rare Interview
scenes.summary: Mina resolves to record the interview verbatim, receives Van Helsing, describes his noble powerful appearance, confirms she kept a written account of Lucy at Whitby, and mystifies him with the shorthand diary before offering the typewritten copy.

scenes.title: Sunshine Opening a Gate
scenes.summary: Mina gives Van Helsing the typewritten diary to save his time; he settles to read it absorbed while she orders lunch, and she returns to find him pacing in blazing excitement, seizing her hands.

scenes.title: Sunshine and Gratitude
scenes.summary: Van Helsing tells Mina her paper is as sunshine to him, solemnly thanks her, and pledges his friendship and all his learning to her and those she loves, calling her one of the lights of life.

scenes.title: You Do Not Know Me
scenes.summary: Mina protests she is praised too much and unknown to him; Van Helsing insists her diary and letter to Lucy reveal her goodness, praises her noble trust, and asks after her husband's health.

scenes.title: A Plea on Her Knees
scenes.summary: Mina tells of Jonathan's upset after Hawkins's death and his shock in town, then breaks down on her knees begging for his cure; Van Helsing raises her tenderly and promises to use all his skill to make Jonathan strong and her life happy.

scenes.title: Entrusting Jonathan's Secret
scenes.summary: After lunch Mina entrusts Van Helsing with the copy of Jonathan's Transylvanian journal to judge for himself, arranges his return visit, and is left thinking as he departs with the papers.

scenes.title: Van Helsing's Pledge of Truth
scenes.summary: Van Helsing writes to Mina that he has read Jonathan's diary, swears it is true, and reassures her that Jonathan's brain and heart are sound and he is a noble, brave man.

scenes.title: Mina's Thanks and Morning Meeting
scenes.summary: Mina thanks Van Helsing for lifting a weight from her mind, reports Jonathan's wire that he returns that night, and asks Van Helsing to come to breakfast at eight instead of lunch.

scenes.title: Jonathan Renewed and an Omen
scenes.summary: Renewed by validation, Jonathan meets Van Helsing, pledges himself against the Count, gives him papers, and sees him off as a newspaper item makes the professor cry out in horror at the departing train.

scenes.title: No Such Thing as Finality
scenes.summary: Seward reopens his diary after declaring it finished, reporting Renfield sane again, Arthur bearing up with Quincey Morris, and his own grief over Lucy healing, until Van Helsing returns from Exeter and bursts in with the Westminster Gazette.

scenes.title: What Poor Lucy Died Of
scenes.summary: Van Helsing points Seward to Hampstead children decoyed away with small punctured throat wounds like Lucy's, rejects nervous prostration and loss of blood as explanation, and rebukes Seward's scientific prejudice against things unseen.

scenes.title: Believe and the Revelation
scenes.summary: Van Helsing lectures Seward on believing the unbelievable, from vampires and astral bodies to undying life, then delivers the shattering reveal that Lucy's wounds were made by Lucy herself.

scenes.title: Anger Calmed by Tenderness
scenes.summary: Seward erupts in anger at Van Helsing's claim about Lucy, striking the table and demanding if he is mad. Van Helsing's tenderness calms him as he denies malice or revenge, explains his indirection as gentleness toward one who loved Lucy, and asks Seward to dare to come with him that night to prove it.

scenes.title: The Key to Prove the Truth
scenes.summary: Seward hesitates at the dreadful proof. Van Helsing argues the logic is simple and harmless if false, then proposes first visiting the wounded hospital child through his friend Dr. Vincent, and then spending the night in Lucy's churchyard, holding up the tomb key obtained from the coffin-man for Arthur.

scenes.title: The Bloofer Lady's Marks
scenes.summary: At the North Hospital they examine the rescued child. Its throat punctures match Lucy's. Vincent blames a bat or rat. Van Helsing warns the child must be strictly watched, but the visit runs late into darkness.

scenes.title: The Tomb by Candlelight
scenes.summary: After dining, Seward and Van Helsing climb into the dark churchyard and slip into the Westenra tomb by candlelight. Amid decay, Van Helsing unscrews the outer coffin and saws open the lead casing, revealing to Seward's shock that Lucy's coffin is empty.

scenes.title: The Divided Watch
scenes.summary: Seward suggests body-snatchers stole the corpse. Van Helsing replaces the lid, locks the tomb, and has them separate to keep watch from opposite sides of the churchyard.

scenes.title: Vigil Among the Yews
scenes.summary: Seward keeps a cold, lonely vigil until a white streak flits among the yews. Van Helsing intercepts it and is found holding a sleeping child. Its throat is unmarked – they were just in time. They abandon it where a policeman will find it and drive home sleepless.

scenes.title: Lucy Beautiful in Death
scenes.summary: Returning by daylight, they find Lucy impossibly beautiful in her coffin, lips redder, teeth sharper. Van Helsing explains trance, vampire bite, and the Un-Dead, and his intent to stake her. To convince Arthur, he defers the killing and plans a night watch alone.

scenes.title: A Lone Watch at the Tomb
scenes.summary: Van Helsing writes an undelivered letter to Seward explaining he goes alone to watch Lucy's tomb, seal it with garlic and crucifix, and face the Count if he comes.

scenes.title: A Morning Return to Doubt
scenes.summary: Van Helsing urges Seward to use the diaries to destroy the great Un-Dead if he falls; next morning, rested, Seward recoils from belief and wonders if Van Helsing is mad.

scenes.title: Buying a Pig in a Poke
scenes.summary: Arthur and Quincey meet Van Helsing, who demands a blind promise to do a grave duty. After debate over honor and faith, he reveals it: go in secret to Kingstead churchyard, enter Lucy's tomb, and open her coffin. Arthur is stunned.

scenes.title: Thorny Paths and the Un-Dead
scenes.summary: Van Helsing warns of thorny paths ahead and asks to be heard. He suggests Lucy may not be truly dead but Un-Dead, and asks permission to cut off her head.

scenes.title: Duty to Others and to the Dead
scenes.summary: Arthur furiously refuses any mutilation of Lucy's body. Van Helsing answers with his solemn duty to the dead and the blood he gave her, moving Arthur to reluctantly agree to come and wait.

scenes.title: Midnight Entry and the Empty Coffin
scenes.summary: Just before midnight the four men enter Lucy's tomb. Van Helsing opens the coffin to show Arthur the proof, and all recoil to find it empty.

scenes.title: Explanation and Plan to Watch
scenes.summary: Challenged by Quincey, Van Helsing swears he did not move the body and recounts the prior empty coffin, the rescued child, and the garlic he removed to allow the Un-Dead to return tonight.

scenes.title: Fresh Air After the Vault
scenes.summary: In the fresh night air outside the vault, the men recover in solemn reflection while Van Helsing crumbles wafer-like biscuit into putty and lays it into the crevices of the tomb door.

scenes.title: Sealing the Tomb With the Host
scenes.summary: Van Helsing reveals he is sealing the tomb with the Host brought from Amsterdam so the Un-Dead cannot enter, and the men hide around the tomb to wait in ghastly suspense.

scenes.title: Lucy the Un-Dead Appears
scenes.summary: A white figure approaches bearing a child and is revealed as Lucy, cruel and voluptuous with blood-stained lips. She discards the child, lures Arthur, and is repelled by Van Helsing's crucifix and barred from her tomb.

scenes.title: Barred Entry and Sorrowful Withdrawal
scenes.summary: Arthur gives anguished consent for Van Helsing's work. The woman passes corporeally through the sealed door, Van Helsing restores the seal, rescues the child, and comforts Arthur as they leave.

scenes.title: Return to the Tomb and Grim Preparations
scenes.summary: The next day the party returns after the funeral, reopens the tomb to find Lucy's beautiful but demonic body, and Van Helsing lays out stake, hammer, knives, and lamp for the terrible rite.

scenes.title: The Lore of the Un-Dead
scenes.summary: Van Helsing explains the lore of the Un-Dead, that Lucy must multiply evil unless freed, and that her soul will be freed if made to rest as true dead. He asks who has the best right to strike, Arthur volunteers, and Van Helsing instructs him to drive the stake through her heart during the prayer for the dead.

scenes.title: The Mercy-Bearing Stake
scenes.summary: Arthur strikes with the stake while the others pray. The Thing in the coffin writhes, screeches, champs its teeth, and spurts blood from the pierced heart, but Arthur drives deeper until the quivering ceases and the body lies still.

scenes.title: The Hammer Falls
scenes.summary: Arthur drops the hammer, reeling with exhaustion and strain. As the others tend to him, they turn to the coffin with startled surprise, and a glad light dispels the horror from Arthur's face.

scenes.title: Restored to True Death
scenes.summary: Lucy lies restored to sweet purity in true death. Arthur is forgiven and comforted by Van Helsing, kisses her, while Van Helsing and Seward complete the rites. They emerge to sunshine, birdsong, and tempered peace.

scenes.title: Vow for the Greater Hunt
scenes.summary: Van Helsing declares one harrowing step done but a greater task remains to stamp out their sorrow's author. All clasp hands in promise to meet and begin the hunt.

scenes.title: The Telegram and the Papers
scenes.summary: At the Berkeley Hotel Van Helsing receives Mina's telegram, rejoices, and hands Seward the typed Harker diaries to study before rushing off to Liverpool Street.

scenes.title: Arrival at the Asylum
scenes.summary: Seward meets Mina at Paddington, brings her with her typewriter by Underground to the asylum, and waits in his study for her to come down.

scenes.title: The Phonograph Bargain
scenes.summary: In Seward's study Mina discovers the phonograph diary, presses to hear of Lucy's death, is refused, then wins his trust and takes the cylinders to copy while he reads her papers.

scenes.title: No One Must Hear Them
scenes.summary: Seward finishes Jonathan and Mina Harker's diaries; Mina enters sad with eyes flushed from crying over his phonograph cylinders. Moved, he fears he distressed her; she says she was touched by his grief speaking through the machine and has typed the words so no one else need hear his heart beat.

scenes.title: No Secrets Amongst Us
scenes.summary: Mina insists Seward's record must be shared as part of Lucy's death and the fight to rid the earth of the monster. Citing her work with Jonathan and Van Helsing, now gone to Whitby, she demands no secrets amongst them; Seward yields and agrees to tell her the rest after dinner.

scenes.title: Typing Lucy's Death
scenes.summary: After dinner Mina listens to the terrible story of Lucy's death, recovers with brandy, types the cylinders in triplicate, and borrows newspapers to hunt for new light.

scenes.title: The Quiet Patient
scenes.summary: Harker arrives energized, the Harkers collate everything chronologically and trace the boxes to the next house; Seward finds Renfield unnaturally sane and orders a watch with strait-waistcoat ready.

scenes.title: Fifty Boxes to Carfax
scenes.summary: Jonathan traces the fifty earth-boxes from Whitby to King's Cross to Carter Paterson to the neglected chapel at Carfax, confirming the Count's hiding place.

scenes.title: Renewed Energy
scenes.summary: With papers ordered, Mina rejoices at Jonathan's renewed volcanic energy and steels herself to feel no pity for the inhuman Thing they hunt.

scenes.title: Comforting Lucy's Suitors
scenes.summary: Mina gives Art and Quincey the compiled narrative, then comforts each grieving suitor in turn for Lucy's sake, becoming their sister and sworn friend.

scenes.title: A House Like Home
scenes.summary: Seward returns home to find the group has studied the transcripts. Over tea, Mina asks to visit Renfield.

scenes.title: The Tidy Cell
scenes.summary: Seward brings Mina to see Renfield, who hastily tidies his cell by swallowing his flies and spiders, then sits watchfully as Mina enters gracefully while Seward stands ready to restrain him.

scenes.title: The Sane Farewell
scenes.summary: Renfield astonishes Seward by speaking to Mina with polished sanity and philosophy, calmly recounting his delusion of prolonging life by consuming living things, then blesses her while praying he may never see her sweet face again.

scenes.title: Meeting at the Station
scenes.summary: Seward meets Van Helsing at the station. Van Helsing arrives energetic and ready to stay, asking eagerly after Mina, Harker, Arthur, and Quincey.

scenes.title: Mina Must Be Spared
scenes.summary: On the drive home Seward briefs Van Helsing. Van Helsing praises Mina as having a man's brain and a woman's heart, but insists she must be excluded from the work after tonight to spare her, and is dismayed to learn Dracula's house is next to Seward's.

scenes.title: Records Complete
scenes.summary: Mina offers her personal record of the day. Van Helsing accepts it, and the collected records are completed for the nine o'clock council.

scenes.title: The Compact
scenes.summary: The council convenes. Van Helsing describes the vampire's strength and cunning, and all join hands in a solemn compact to destroy him.

scenes.title: Lore of the Nosferatu
scenes.summary: Van Helsing details the vampire's powers, limitations, sacred repellents, and reveals the enemy as the historic Voivode Dracula.

scenes.title: Shot in the Dark
scenes.summary: A pistol shot shatters the window. Morris confesses he fired at a large bat perched on the sill, which escaped into the wood.

scenes.title: Mina Set Aside
scenes.summary: The plan is set to trace and sterilize the earth-boxes. Mina is told her part is over, and the men leave for Carfax while she pretends to sleep.

scenes.title: An Urgent Summons
scenes.summary: Just before leaving for Carfax, Seward is urgently summoned by Renfield and the whole party goes down to see him.

scenes.title: A Plea for Freedom
scenes.summary: Lucid and courtly, Renfield introduces his visitors and argues eloquently for immediate release, but refuses to give his true reason and is denied.

scenes.title: Frantic Plea on His Knees
scenes.summary: As Seward moves to leave, Renfield rushes toward him and turns imploring, then collapses into frantic, tearful supplication on his knees when his plea is refused.

scenes.title: Remember That I Warned You
scenes.summary: Renfield begs to be sent away to save his soul from guilt, is sternly ordered to bed and subsides into calm obedience, then quietly asks Seward to remember that he did what he could to convince him.

scenes.title: Debate After Renfield
scenes.summary: At dawn Jonathan notes Mina strong and left behind. The men debrief Renfield's plea for freedom in the study, debating if he is sane, earnest, or the Count's tool, and resolve to take no chances.

scenes.title: Armed Entry Into Carfax
scenes.summary: The party crosses to Carfax at moonlight. Van Helsing arms each man with crucifix, garlic, revolver, lamp and Host, then Seward picks the lock and they enter, feeling watched.

scenes.title: Dust and the Chapel Stench
scenes.summary: Lamps flicker over deep dust and cobwebs, with hobnail tracks and used keys. Jonathan leads to the chapel, which exhales a corrupt, bloody, earthy stench of the Count, which they force themselves to endure.

scenes.title: Twenty-Nine Boxes and a Face
scenes.summary: They count only twenty-nine earth-boxes left of fifty. Jonathan glimpses what seems the Count's red-eyed face in the dark passage, but investigation finds solid wall and no hiding place.

scenes.title: The Phosphorescent Swarm
scenes.summary: Morris discovers a phosphorescent mass of swarming rats. Godalming opens the iron-bound outer door and whistles for help, but the three terriers halt howling at the threshold as rats multiply in thousands.

scenes.title: The Terriers Rout the Rats
scenes.summary: Godalming carries the terriers inside and they rout the rats. Dread lifts, the party locks the chapel and searches the dusty, empty house with no further uneasiness.

scenes.title: Dawn Success and Vow of Silence
scenes.summary: At dawn Van Helsing locks up, triumphs that Mina was spared horror and that beasts resist the Count's spirit power. Back home Jonathan finds Mina pale asleep and vows to seal their work from her.

scenes.title: Van Helsing Requests Renfield Visit
scenes.summary: At noon Van Helsing, cheered by last night's work, asks to visit Renfield alone for philosophical talk. Seward agrees and warns him not to be misled by Renfield's talk of consuming life, noting his mouth was still foul with flies and spiders when he spoke to Mina.

scenes.title: Van Helsing Rebuffed
scenes.summary: Van Helsing returns quickly, rebuffed: Renfield sat sullen and called him an old fool and thickheaded Dutchman. Van Helsing takes comfort that Mina is out of the affair, Seward heartily agrees women have no place in it, and the men disperse to confer and trace the earth-boxes.

scenes.title: Mina Shut Out
scenes.summary: Mina feels hurt at being kept in the dark after years of confidence, weeps over Jonathan's tender silence, blames her Whitby visit for Lucy's fate, and resolves to hide tears and keep her journal.

scenes.title: Pillar of Mist and Drugged Sleep
scenes.summary: Mina recalls mist stealing to the house, Renfield's struggle, then a vivid dream of fog pouring through the door into a whirling pillar with red eyes and a livid face. Exhausted next day, she takes a sleeping draught and fears losing power to wake.

scenes.title: The Trail of the Boxes
scenes.summary: Harker traces the Carfax boxes to Smollet, who reveals six boxes went to Chicksand Street and six to Jamaica Lane. Smollet offers to track fellow carter Sam Bloxam. Harker returns home weary to find Mina pale and shut out of the work.

scenes.title: Hunting Sam Bloxam
scenes.summary: Harker receives Bloxam's misspelled address and follows it from Walworth to Poplar. After a long search at a cold-storage building he finds Bloxam, who admits two journeys from Carfax to Piccadilly with nine heavy boxes.

scenes.title: Nine Boxes in Piccadilly
scenes.summary: Bloxam describes the white-moustached old man of uncanny strength who met him at Purfleet and Piccadilly and carried boxes unaided. With his description of a high stone-front house, Harker locates the dusty, long-untenanted Piccadilly mansion.

scenes.title: The House Agents Stonewall
scenes.summary: Harker learns the Piccadilly house was lately for sale through Mitchell, Sons & Candy. The clerk stonewalls with 'It is sold, sir' until Harker invokes Lord Godalming, securing a promise to write. Exhausted, Harker returns to Purfleet.

scenes.title: Night Council at Purfleet
scenes.summary: After putting Mina to bed, Harker reads his diary to the men. Van Helsing hails progress, but Morris and Godalming warn that burglaring a Piccadilly mansion is far riskier than Carfax. They resolve to wait for Mitchell's letter.

scenes.title: Renfield Commands Destiny
scenes.summary: Seward finds Renfield exalted, commanding destiny and disdaining souls while insisting he wants only life. Pressed about Enoch and God, Renfield grows cunning, evasive, and falls into dogged silence.

scenes.title: What About Souls?
scenes.summary: Seward torments Renfield with images of buzzing souls of flies, spiders, and elephants. Renfield breaks down, rages against talk of souls, begs not to be strait-waistcoated, then turns gratefully calm.

scenes.title: A New Scheme of Terror
scenes.summary: Seward deduces Renfield expects a higher human life from the Count and dreads its soul-burden. Van Helsing finds Renfield gaily singing and catching flies again, yielding nothing. They resolve to watch him that night.

scenes.title: The Purchaser Revealed
scenes.summary: Mitchell, Sons & Candy confirm No. 347 Piccadilly was sold by Winter-Suffield's executors to a foreign nobleman, Count de Ville, who paid in notes over the counter.

scenes.title: Quiet Before the Yell
scenes.summary: Seward posts a night watch on Renfield, who prays loudly then sleeps soundly. By day the hunters prepare horses and research while Renfield stays ominously quiet, until a wild yell and blood on the floor summon Seward urgently.

scenes.title: Renfield Lying in Blood
scenes.summary: Seward finds Renfield on the floor in a pool of blood from severe face wounds, with his right side paralysed. The attendant is baffled how Renfield could have both beaten his face and broken his back.

scenes.title: Van Helsing Called to Operate
scenes.summary: Seward summons Van Helsing, who arrives hurriedly and asks to be left alone with the patient. After sending Simmons away, they examine Renfield and find a depressed skull fracture through the motor area requiring operation.

scenes.title: Vigil and Emergency Operation
scenes.summary: Arthur and Quincey join the grim vigil as Van Helsing waits to trephine. Agonizing suspense builds while Renfield hovers between stupor and death. With no time left, Van Helsing operates above the ear, and Renfield suddenly opens his eyes and speaks.

scenes.title: It Was No Dream But Reality
scenes.summary: Revived with water and brandy, Renfield insists it was no dream but grim reality. Feeling he has only minutes to live, he begins his confession of the night after Seward left him, when the Count came solid in the mist to his window with fierce eyes and laughing red mouth.

scenes.title: Come In, Lord and Master
scenes.summary: Renfield recounts the temptation: flies and moths, then thousands of red-eyed rats offered with all red blood and lives if he would worship the Count, until in a red cloud he opened the sash and invited his Lord and Master in.

scenes.title: Renfield's Final Fight
scenes.summary: Renfield explains his change of heart after seeing Mina drained pale by the Count. When the Count returned that night he grappled the mist with madman's strength to protect her, until the burning eyes overpowered him and flung him down to die.

scenes.title: Horror in the Harkers' Bedroom
scenes.summary: Realizing the Count is with Mina now, the men arm themselves and rush to the Harkers' locked door. Breaking it in, they discover the Count forcing Mina to drink from his breast while Jonathan lies stupored. Crosses and Wafer drive him back into mist that slips under the door.

scenes.title: Grief and Vows After the Attack
scenes.summary: Van Helsing wakes the stupored Jonathan while Mina wails in terror and shame. Jonathan vows nothing will come between them as Van Helsing reassures her with his crucifix. Seward recounts to Jonathan what they witnessed.

scenes.title: The Burned Manuscripts and Renfield's Death
scenes.summary: Arthur reports that the Count burned all the manuscripts and threw the phonograph cylinders on the fire, Seward takes comfort that another copy survives in the safe, and Arthur then reveals that Renfield is dead.

scenes.title: The Bat's Westward Flight
scenes.summary: Quincey reports seeing a bat rise from Renfield's window and flap westward away from Carfax, concluding that dawn is too close for the Count to return that night.

scenes.title: Mina Tells Her Binding
scenes.summary: At Van Helsing's urging, Mina describes the thin mist, Jonathan's unnatural sleep, the Count's threat, drinking her blood, and forcing her to drink his blood to bind her to his call. Dawn breaks on Jonathan's greyed face and a miserable house keeping watch.

scenes.title: Jonathan Writes in Despair
scenes.summary: Jonathan writes in his journal at six o'clock to keep from madness before the half-hour meeting, recording the resolve to eat so they can work, and Mina's tearful insistence on trust and faith amid dread of the end.

scenes.title: Renfield Found Dead
scenes.summary: Seward reports Renfield found heaped on the floor below with face bruised and crushed and neck broken, the attendant having heard cries of God and a fall, and explains the plan to certify death by misadventure to avoid an inquest into the truth.

scenes.title: No Concealment From Mina
scenes.summary: The group agrees Mina must be told everything with no concealment. Mina declares that if she senses harm to those she loves coming from herself, she will die, and Van Helsing solemnly charges her that she must not die by any hand, least of all her own, until Dracula is truly dead.

scenes.title: Mina's Promise to Live
scenes.summary: Mina promises to strive to live until the horror has passed, strengthening the group, who then give her charge of all the papers and records as before.

scenes.title: Planning the Day's Hunt
scenes.summary: Van Helsing lays out the day's hunt while Dracula is confined to mortal form. He calms Jonathan's impatience with a lawful locksmith ruse to enter Piccadilly, and Morris and Godalming plan discreet cabs and carriages for Walworth and Mile End.

scenes.title: Mina Insists All Strength Must Go
scenes.summary: Mina shows growing interest despite looking pale and drawn, frightening Jonathan with memories of Lucy. When the group plans to clear Carfax then enter Piccadilly in force, Jonathan wants to stay to guard Mina, but she insists all strength must go against the Count and persuades him to join them.

scenes.title: Van Helsing Recalls the Banquet
scenes.summary: Van Helsing delays their start by noting Dracula banqueted heavily and will sleep late, thoughtlessly recalling Mina's trauma. Mina breaks down briefly, forgives him, then urges them to eat breakfast to be strong before going.

scenes.title: The Wafer Burns Her Brow
scenes.summary: After a strained effort at cheerful breakfast, Van Helsing arms the party and touches Mina's forehead with the Sacred Wafer, which sears her flesh like white-hot metal, drawing a fearful scream and leaving her kneeling in abasement with hair over her face.

scenes.title: The Oath to Lift Her Sorrow
scenes.summary: Mina wails herself unclean and marked till Judgment Day; Van Helsing comforts her that the scar will pass when God lifts their burden, then all kneel holding hands and swear to lift her sorrow before Jonathan bids her farewell and the men set out.

scenes.title: Sterilizing Carfax
scenes.summary: Jonathan resolves Mina shall not face vampirism alone. The men sterilize the Carfax earth-boxes with the Host, see Mina waving from the asylum window, and catch the train, writing en route.

scenes.title: Entering the Piccadilly Lair
scenes.summary: In London the party watches Godalming and Morris use a locksmith to open the Piccadilly house unchallenged. Inside they find eight earth-boxes, sterilize them, and discover deeds, correspondence, and keys, sending Godalming and Morris east and south while the rest wait for Dracula.

scenes.title: Waiting and Van Helsing's Lecture
scenes.summary: While waiting for Godalming and Morris, Van Helsing keeps the party occupied with anxious talk. He lectures on Dracula's growing child-brain, his experiments with moving earth-boxes, and that all lairs but one will soon be sterilized.

scenes.title: Telegram Warning from Mina
scenes.summary: A telegram from Mina warns that Dracula has left Carfax hurriedly toward the south. Harker exults at a coming meeting, but Van Helsing cautions him, noting the vampire is limited till sunset and urging restraint.

scenes.title: The Hunters Reunite
scenes.summary: Godalming and Morris return reporting both Bermondsey and Mile End lairs destroyed. Van Helsing deduces Dracula's river-crossing route and readies weapons as a key is softly inserted in the hall door.

scenes.title: Ambush in Position
scenes.summary: Quincey Morris instinctively takes command and silently places Van Helsing, Harker and Seward behind the door and Godalming and himself by the window as the Count's slow, careful steps approach along the hall.

scenes.title: Count Repelled and Leap
scenes.summary: Dracula bursts into the room with panther-like speed, Harker slashes his coat with a kukri spilling banknotes and gold, the men's crucifixes drive him back, and he dives under Harker's arm and leaps through the window into the yard below.

scenes.title: Defiance and Failed Pursuit
scenes.summary: From the stable door Dracula taunts the men with revenge and claims their loved women, then bolts it behind him; Van Helsing burns his title-deeds and papers while Godalming, Morris and Harker's pursuit through the yard and mews fails.

scenes.title: Mina's Plea for Pity
scenes.summary: Defeated and fearing sunset, the party returns to protect Mina. After supper and recounting, Mina pleads that they pity Dracula's soul even while destroying him. Harker erupts with hate, Mina rebukes him, and all weep before the lovers are left alone under guard.

scenes.title: Midnight Watch
scenes.summary: Late at night Harker broods on the last earth-box and his faith in Mina. Woken by Mina alarmed at a sound in the corridor, he finds Morris on guard outside, and Mina falls back asleep comforted by brave men.

scenes.title: Call for Hypnosis Before Dawn
scenes.summary: Before dawn Mina urgently calls for Van Helsing to hypnotize her. He arrives in dressing-gown with the others gathering, fixes her gaze, and brings her into trance as daylight approaches.

scenes.title: Voices on the Water
scenes.summary: Under hypnosis Mina answers she sees darkness but hears lapping water, stamping men, and capstan chain. Van Helsing and the watchers realize she is on a ship, until sunrise breaks the trance and she awakes asking what she said.

scenes.title: Flight by Sea and a Dread Purpose
scenes.summary: Van Helsing explains Dracula has taken his last box aboard ship to flee London. When Mina asks why pursue him, he solemnly says because his mark is on her throat and time is dreaded, and she faints at the horror.

scenes.title: Van Helsing's Orders
scenes.summary: Van Helsing leaves a phonograph message ordering Jonathan to stay and guard Mina, revealing the Count has fled back to Transylvania and promising the fight has only begun.

scenes.title: Fragile Comfort
scenes.summary: Jonathan reads the message to Mina and feels brief comfort in daylight, but Mina's scar and their re-reading of the diaries keep fear alive beneath a fragile hope.

scenes.title: Tracing the Czarina Catherine
scenes.summary: At the evening report meeting, Van Helsing recounts how, certain Dracula would flee by the Black Sea for the Danube, they checked Lloyd's and found only one Black-Sea-bound ship on the tide, the Czarina Catherine for Varna, and then questioned men at Doolittle's Wharf.

scenes.title: The Thin Man and the Fog
scenes.summary: The wharf men describe a hurrying tall, thin, pale man in black who paid the captain well, himself loaded a great box aboard, and returned at full tide; a dense fog held only around the ship until he boarded, then lifted and the Czarina Catherine sailed on the ebb.

scenes.title: The Plan for Varna
scenes.summary: Van Helsing concludes the Count is at sea with fog at his command for the Danube mouth, but they can travel faster by land to meet him; the box is consigned to agent Ristics at Varna, and they must strike while he lies helpless in the box between sunrise and sunset.

scenes.title: Necessary Pursuit
scenes.summary: Mina questions pursuing the Count, and Van Helsing erupts in passionate resolve, warning that her infection means she will become like him unless they act, and that the tiger man-eater will never stop.

scenes.title: Peace Shattered
scenes.summary: The council adjourns to sleep on a plan; Mina feels momentary peace until she sees her red forehead mark in the mirror and knows she is still unclean.

scenes.title: Morning Cheer and Shared Fear
scenes.summary: Seward notes forced cheerfulness at early breakfast, broken only by the scar on Mina's forehead. He confides his dread that her tongue is tied by the Count's poison, and alone with Van Helsing learns the Professor shares his fear that Mina is changing and that the Count may compel her to reveal their plans.

scenes.title: The Painful Resolve to Exclude Her
scenes.summary: Van Helsing resolves that Mina must be kept ignorant of their intent and excluded from their council lest the Count read her mind. Seward agrees to spare him doubt, and Van Helsing withdraws to prepare himself for the painful task.

scenes.title: Plan of Campaign
scenes.summary: Relieved by Mina's absence, the men plan to reach Varna before the ship, arm with Winchesters, and pointedly exclude Harker to guard his wife, silencing disclosure with a finger to lips.

scenes.title: Watching Mina Sleep
scenes.summary: Jonathan is left dazed after the morning meeting, puzzled by Mina's determination to withdraw, and watches her sleeping calmly and happily like a child.

scenes.title: The Holy Promise
scenes.summary: Mina wakes and makes Jonathan swear holily never to tell her the plans against the Count while the scar remains, shutting a door between them, before a strangely bright and gay evening.

scenes.title: Mina Must Go
scenes.summary: At sunrise Mina summons Van Helsing to declare she must go with them, for the Count can summon her and she can serve them through hypnosis; he accepts her wisdom.

scenes.title: Ready for Varna
scenes.summary: The men resolve to board the ship at Varna, rose-branch the box and destroy the Count, settle wills and travel, as sunset brings Mina's uneasiness and Jonathan is called away.

scenes.title: Sunset Freedom Gathering
scenes.summary: Seward records for Harker as the group gathers before sunset, when Mina regains her free self after a struggle, and draws everyone close to speak.

scenes.title: The Dreadful Vow
scenes.summary: Mina solemnly asks all, even her husband, to promise to kill her with stake and beheading if she turns, and warns they must act instantly as she may then be leagued with the enemy.

scenes.title: Burial Service Reading
scenes.summary: Mina asks Jonathan to read the Burial Service over her; he reads brokenly amid kneeling friends, bringing strange comfort as her freedom fades.

scenes.title: Watch at Varna
scenes.summary: The party races to Varna on the Orient Express to await the Czarina Catherine; hypnotic reports show only sea and wind, and they plan to board her by day and destroy the Count.

scenes.title: Ship Reported, Fevered Wait
scenes.summary: News that the ship passed the Dardanelles sparks battle excitement; they retire to rise ready, while Seward notes Mina's lethargy and sharpening danger.

scenes.title: Lethargy and Mounting Fear
scenes.summary: The ship fails to arrive and Mina sinks into troubling lethargy; Van Helsing fears souls can act strangely in trance and plans a fuller sunset questioning.

scenes.title: Diverted to Galatz
scenes.summary: A telegram reveals the ship has bypassed them for Galatz; after stunned reactions, Mina supplies train times and Van Helsing dispatches the men to prepare pursuit.

scenes.title: The Count's Escape Trick
scenes.summary: Alone with Seward, Van Helsing theorizes the Count read Mina's mind in trance, learned they were in Varna, fled to Galatz, and cut her off, believing himself free.

scenes.title: Child-Brain and Hope
scenes.summary: From Harker's journal Van Helsing expounds the Count's child-criminal habit of repeating past flight; Mina sees her soul is freer, yet can still track him at sunrise and sunset.

scenes.title: Sunset Trance on the Train
scenes.summary: On the night train to Galatz the party gathers at sunset for Mina's hypnosis. With unusual difficulty she reports still water, voices, oars, a gun, tramping feet and blowing air, then wakes asking sweetly for tea while the men grasp its ominous meaning.

scenes.title: Counsel and a Fruitless Dawn
scenes.summary: Van Helsing explains the Count is close to land but not yet ashore, vulnerable by day if still boxed. At dawn Mina can say only that all is dark with lapping water and creaking wood, and the party rushes toward Galatz in agony, already hours late.

scenes.title: The Fading Power
scenes.summary: At sunset Mina resists hypnosis and speaks enigmatically of cold wind, strange tongues, falling water and wolves, then shakes in palsy. Next morning she fails completely, remembering nothing after sunrise, as the train nears Galatz in feverish anxiety.

scenes.title: Arrival in Galatz
scenes.summary: Arrived in Galatz, the forces divide: Morris sees Mina to the hotel, Godalming seeks the Vice-Consul, Jonathan and the doctors go to the shipping agent. The officials are absent or sick, leaving only a clerk's willing but thin help.

scenes.title: The Captain's Tale
