scenes.summary: Aboard the Czarina Catherine, Captain Donelson tells of an uncannily swift, fog-bound voyage from London, grumbling Romanian sailors, and a great box marked Galatz via Varna taken before sunrise by a man with English papers, receipt signed Immanuel Hildesheim.

scenes.title: Dead End at Skinsky's Murder
scenes.summary: Hildesheim admits clearing the box before sunrise for Skinsky, dealer with the Slovaks. Skinsky has vanished, then is found murdered in St. Peter's churchyard with his throat torn open. The box is somewhere on the water, and the party returns heavy-hearted to consider trusting Mina again.

scenes.title: Mina Types While the Men Rest
scenes.summary: Mina asks the exhausted, dispirited men to rest for half an hour while she types up everything, grateful for the Traveller's typewriter, as she watches Jonathan collapsed in pain on the sofa and resolves to help him.

scenes.title: Mina Makes Her Discovery
scenes.summary: Mina gets the remaining papers from Van Helsing and studies them without prejudice while the men rest, finds a discovery confirmed by the maps, and prepares her memorandum to lay before the party.

scenes.title: By Road, by Rail, by Water
scenes.summary: Mina reasons the Count, confined helpless in his box between dawn and sunset, must be carried by someone, and by exclusion rejects road for curiosity, customs, and pursuit and rail for delay without a keeper, leaving water as safest despite its danger, so they must ascertain what water.

scenes.title: The River Route to the Castle
scenes.summary: Mina traces his feint invoice to Varna, swift run of the Czarina Catherine to Galatz, and handover through Hildesheim to Skinsky, argues Skinsky was chosen for isolated Slovak river carriage and then murdered, and from map and trance sounds of water and creaking wood concludes the box is in an open boat poled upstream, likely the Sereth to the Bistritza toward the Borgo Pass.

scenes.title: Council of War
scenes.summary: Hailed as teacher for her hypnotic clue, Mina's plan becomes a council of war: Godalming by steam launch upriver, Morris and Seward on horseback along the bank, Van Helsing with Mina overland to the Castle. Jonathan protests hotly at taking Mina toward Dracula, and Van Helsing calms him by arguing only destroying the Count and sanctifying his nest can save her.

scenes.title: Hasty Arming and Farewell
scenes.summary: Jonathan yields to God's hands while Mina records their hasty equipping with Godalming's and Morris's money: steam launch, horses, maps, arms and furs, and Van Helsing's night train to Veresti for the Borgo. She ends with a fearful, tearless goodbye to Jonathan.

scenes.title: Pursuit by Steam Launch
scenes.summary: By furnace-light Jonathan and Godalming race up the Sereth into the Bistritza, overhauling boats under a Romanian flag, learning a double-crewed boat passed before Fundu. Cold, sleeplessness and engine strain wear them as they push toward Strasba hoping to join the horsemen.

scenes.title: Hard Riding on the Bank
scenes.summary: Three hard days on horseback, Seward and Morris press after the launch, hearing at Fundu it went up the Bistritza and was delayed forcing the rapids. With snow threatening, they push harder, knowing their help may soon be needed.

scenes.title: Veresti - Into the Enemy's Country
scenes.summary: Mina and Van Helsing reach Veresti, where hypnosis yields only dark and quiet. They buy carriage, horses, furs and provisions for the 70-mile drive to the Borgo Pass, commending Jonathan to God as they prepare to start into the enemy's country.

scenes.title: Kind Horses and the Evil Eye
scenes.summary: Mina records a rapid eastward drive with willing horses and generous peasants. After a serving woman reacts to the scar on her forehead as the evil eye, she hides it beneath hat and veil, while the tireless Van Helsing hurries toward Bistritz and his sunset hypnosis confirms Dracula is still on the river.

scenes.title: The Wild Road to the Borgo Pass
scenes.summary: Mina and Van Helsing take turns driving through cold and oppressive air into wilder Carpathian country. Morning hypnosis suggests the river is changing as Dracula ascends, and with a rude four-in-hand they press on to reach the Borgo Pass by daylight, cheering each other while Mina prays for guidance and for Jonathan.

scenes.title: Cold Record and Jonathan's Byroad
scenes.summary: Van Helsing takes up the record in bitter cold at the Borgo Pass, noting Mina has slept all day, lost appetite, and made no diary entry. At dawn she briefly yields to hypnosis with only darkness and swirling water, then shows strange zeal to find Jonathan's byroad. She sleeps on through the long climb until he cannot wake her.

scenes.title: Failing Trance by the Night Fire
scenes.summary: At sunset Van Helsing rouses Mina but fails altogether to hypnotize her. By the night fire she seems bright and well, yet eats apart from him, and his watch keeps lapsing into sleep. By morning hypnosis fails again and she sinks into a heavy, unnatural sleep that leaves him fearing the vampire taint is growing.

scenes.title: The Holy Circle Before the Castle
scenes.summary: Pushing through wild precipices toward the castle hill, Van Helsing finds Mina unwakeable. At twilight before the castle he feeds the horses, makes fire, and draws a Holy circle with the Wafer around her. She cannot cross it, proving her soul still safe though her body is in danger.

scenes.title: Night Siege by the Sisters
scenes.summary: Through the snow-mist night the three female vampires materialize outside the ring, calling Mina sister. Van Helsing holds them off with fire and Wafer while horses cower and Mina smiles strangely. At dawn they melt toward the castle and he finds Mina in deep sleep and the horses dead.

scenes.title: Pursuers Converging
scenes.summary: After the night of terror, Jonathan records pursuit on horseback after the launch failure, and Seward records sighting the Szgany leiter-wagon fleeing the river in light snow with wolves howling. All parties are riding to a final convergence.

scenes.title: Entering the Chapel and Sealing Dracula's Tomb
scenes.summary: Leaving Mina asleep in the Holy circle, Van Helsing breaks into the castle and finds his way to the chapel. Oppressed by fumes and tempted by the voluptuous beauty of the three vampire women in their tombs, he is roused by Mina's distant wail, locates all three sisters and Dracula's great tomb, which he seals with Wafer to banish the Count forever.

scenes.title: Destroying the Sisters and Returning to Mina
scenes.summary: Nerved by Mina's cry, Van Helsing stakes and beheads the three vampire sisters, watching their bodies dissolve to native dust. He then bars the castle entrances against the Count's return and goes back to Mina, who wakes to see what he has endured.

scenes.title: Watch on the Snowy Waste
scenes.summary: Cured of ruddy vampire sleep but weak, Mina goes east with Van Helsing to meet her husband. From a rock hollow sheltered by a new circle they spot the cart with the great chest, pursued from south and north by Seward, Morris, Jonathan and Godalming, while wolves gather as sunset nears.

scenes.title: Halt: The Rush for the Cart
scenes.summary: Surrounded by rifles, the gypsies halt but draw weapons and ring the cart. Jonathan and Quincey force their way through knives to the cart, hurl the great box to the ground, Morris wounded in the side, and together prize off the lid.

scenes.title: Sunset: Dracula Crumbles to Dust
scenes.summary: Dracula lies pale in the box with vindictive eyes turning triumphant at the sinking sun. At sunset Jonathan shears through his throat as Morris plunges his bowie into his heart, and the body crumbles to dust with a look of peace.

scenes.title: Release and a Gallant Death
scenes.summary: The castle stands against the red sky as gypsies flee and wolves follow them. Mortally wounded in the side, Morris declares himself happy, points to Mina's forehead now stainless in the sunset light as proof the curse is lifted, receives their Amen, and dies smiling.

scenes.title: Seven Years After - Peace and Remembrance
scenes.summary: Seven years after the events, Jonathan Harker reflects with peaceful, nostalgic joy. He notes his son Quincey, named for Quincey Morris, recounts a return pilgrimage to a now-empty Transylvania, and describes re-reading their collected papers at home with friends, closing with Van Helsing's tribute to Mina's bravery.
